pages.content:
# Best AI Agents: Evidence-Backed Guide for Real Workflows

A useful AI-agent recommendation begins with a specific workflow rather than a universal winner. Define the task, the data it can read, the tools it can call, the actions it can take, the human owner, the expected output, the acceptable failure rate, and the rollback path. Products should then be compared against the same test case with current primary-source documentation.

## What to verify

Check the execution surface, integration model, permission boundaries, auditability, pricing model, usage limits, deployment options, data handling, support model, and change-management process. Separate vendor-documented facts from editorial interpretation. Do not convert a marketing claim into a score unless the underlying evidence and scoring rule are both recorded.

## How to test

Use a reversible pilot. Give each candidate the same representative task, record completion quality and failure modes, review every proposed change, and keep high-impact actions behind human approval. Re-run repository tests, policy checks, or business validations before accepting agent output.

## Evidence policy

Historical Google Search visibility preserves this URL but is not factual evidence. Product details must be rechecked against the listed primary sources when material claims change. Missing evidence means HOLD rather than invented specificity.
